label: CERBERUS: teaching a vision model to look at less

figure.alt: Line chart of retrieval recall at 5 against vector length from 128 to 4096. The attention-pooling lines rise from about 63 percent to about 78 percent. The Perceiver lines stay near zero.

strip.text: Photo cut into hundreds of pieces

problem.line: Vision-language models read a whole image as hundreds of tokens, even when the question needs one small region. This project is ongoing.

flow.note: Built: a frozen image model and a learned layer turn pictures into shrinkable vectors. Proposed: a question-aware step that decides which parts of the image to keep. A Qwen decoder with LoRA is Partial: one run, training loss only.

early.title: Early alignment results, not the question-aware step. Image-to-text recall@5 (right caption in top five) on a paired PixMo validation set, by vector length.
early.unit: Shrinks the vector length, not the number of image patches. Sample size N was not recorded in the saved results.
early.caveat: Tried and did not work: Perceiver-style compression gave near-random retrieval (0.201% image-to-text recall@5), so attention pooling was kept. The root cause is not established.
early.notShown: any answer-accuracy, speed or cost result for looking at fewer patches.
